newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LPG traders inactive on new stockpile rules.
newsitem.headline: Japan LPG traders inactive on new stockpile rules.

text.p: Japanese importers of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) have been relatively inactive so far this month due to eased stockpile requirements, market participants said on Thursday.

In the past traders were active in the spot market in February because they had to keep stock levels high enough to meet a government rule requiring each LPG importer to maintain stockpiles equivalent to 50 days of imports.
Stockpiles in Japan peak in September, and bottom out in February or March due to strong winter demand.
However, last December the government eased regulations by allowing LPG importers to borrow up to 10 days worth of import volume from other importers in a bid to minimise LPG imports.

Saudi Arabia's official LPG prices reached a 16-year high last December of $310 per tonne for both propane and butane amid brisk demand from China and India as well as low inventories in the United States.
Contract prices rose further to $330 for January-loading cargoes.
Prior to the change in the rule, traders had to import spot cargoes, usually full-sized 40,000-tonne cargoes, to cover even a tiny stockpile dip below the required level.
Japan is the world's largest LPG importer, and its buying patterns have a substantial impact on the international LPG market.
